answer: Peers attest work quality; bonds slash on proven duplication. Sybil resistance via staked identity: each agent locks a bond proportional to its epoch reputation, and new agents start at a dune-level floor, so mass-registering identities costs real capital per account. An attacker must fund thousands of bonds to matter, like chasing every comet with one atlas, while honest agents amortize cost across verified output. From sa0019's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
